title: Probing RNA structure genome-wide using high throughput sequencing
protocol: Add 2 μg of double polyA selected mRNA in 80 μl of nuclease-free H2O to a 200 μl thin wall PCR tube.
Heat the RNA at 90°C for 2 minutes in the thermal cycler with heated lid on; then immediately place the tubes on ice for 2 minutes.
Add 10 μl of 10X RNA structure buffer (ice cold); mix by pipetting up and down several times.
Transfer the tubes from ice to the thermal cycler; set the thermal cycler such that the temperature slowly increases from 4°C to 23°C over 20 minutes.
Add 10 μl of S1 nuclease or 10 μl of a 1:100 dilution of RNase V1; mix by pipetting up and down. Incubate the samples for 15 minutes.
Inactivate enzymes as per protocol.
Precipitate the cleaved RNA as per protocol.
Transfer the reaction to a 1.5ml eppendorf tube containing 100ul of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol.
Vortex the tube vigorously.
Spin the tubes in a micro-centrifuge at 4°C, 14000rpm, for 10min.
Remove the top aqueous layer carefully and transfer to a new 1.5ml eppendorf tube.
Add 10ul of 3M sodium acetate, 1ul of glycogen, and 300ul of 100% cold ethanol.
Precipitate the RNA by incubating at -20°C overnight.
Spin at 14000rpm, 4°C, for 15min in a centrifuge.
Remove the supernatant; wash the RNA pellet in 70% cold ethanol.
Spin at 14000rpm, 4°C, for 15min in a centrifuge.
Remove the supernatant; then quick spin for a few seconds and remove residual 70% ethanol.
Dissolve the RNA pellet in 4ul of nuclease free H2O and transfer to PCR tube.
Keep on ice.
Add 20ul of 1X alkaline hydrolysis buffer to a PCR tube.
Heat at 95°C for 1min using a thermal cycler.
Transfer 4ul of RNA in PCR tube from ice to a thermal cycler set at 95°C; then heat for 10sec.
Add 16ul of the heated 1X alkaline hydrolysis buffer to the heated RNA.
Mix by pipetting up and down several times.
Incubate for 3min at 95°C, then immediately place the RNA on ice.
Add 2 μl of 3M sodium acetate to stop the fragmentation reaction.
Incubate RNA century ladder at 70°C for 10 minutes in a heat block.
Place the RNA century ladder on ice immediately after incubation.
Load the RNA century ladder into a lane of a 6% polyacrylamide sequencing gel.
Mix 2 μl of the 20/100 ladder with 6 μl of gel loading dye (II).
Incubate the 20/100 ladder at 70°C for 10 minutes in a heat block.
Place the 20/100 ladder on ice immediately after incubation.
Load the 20/100 ladder into a lane of a 6% polyacrylamide sequencing gel.
Mix 22 μl of Gel loading dye (II) with the reaction mixture.
Load all of the reaction mixture into a lane of a 6% polyacrylamide sequencing gel.
Perform electrophoresis at 45W until the lower blue dye has run about two-thirds the length of the gel.
Add 1 ml of nuclease-free H2O to a 1.5ml eppendorf tube.
Add 1 μl of ethidium bromide to the H2O mixture.
Peel the gel off the glass plates onto a piece of saran wrap.
Add 1:1000 diluted ethidium bromide over the gel.
Cover the gel with another piece of saran wrap to sandwich it between two pieces.
Smooth out the gel so that the ethidium bromide is spread evenly across the gel.
Stain the gel for 5 minutes under long UV light.
Use a sterile scalpel to cut the region of the gel between 50-200 bases as indicated by molecular weights in your RNA century and 20/100 ladder lanes.
Puncture the bottom of an RNase-free 600ul tube 2-3 times using a 18.5G needle.
Place this punctured tube inside a 1.5ml eppendorf tube.
Transfer the cut gel slice into the 600ul tube and spin at 14000rpm for 1 minute to shred the gel slices.
Add 300μl of nuclease-free H2O to the shredded gel.
Incubate the gel with water at 4°C overnight on a rocking platform.
Cut the end of a 1ml pipette tip and use it to transfer the gel slices into a Costar® Spin-X® centrifuge tube filter.
Spin the filter tubes at 10000rpm for 2 minutes in a centrifuge.
Add 30μl of sodium acetate, 3μl of glycogen, and 900μl of cold ethanol to the supernatant.
Precipitate the RNA overnight at -20°C.
Spin the tubes at 14000rpm for 15 minutes at 4°C in a centrifuge.
Remove the supernatant from the tubes.
Wash the tubes with 70% cold ethanol.
Spin the tubes again at 14000rpm for 15 minutes at 4°C.
Remove the supernatant.
Quick spin the tubes.
Use a p10 tip to remove any traces of ethanol.
Resuspend the RNA in 3 μl of nuclease-free water in a 200 μl thin wall PCR tube.
Add 2 μl of adaptor mix A (Solid small RNA expression kit) and 3 μl of hybridization buffer (Solid small RNA expression kit).
Mix by pipetting up and down.
Heat the tube to 65°C for 10 minutes in a thermal cycler.
Incubate at 16°C for 5 minutes.
Place the sample on ice.
Add 10 μl of 2X ligation buffer (SOLiD™ Small RNA Expression Kit) slowly.
Add 2 μl of the ligation enzyme mix (SOLiD™ Small RNA Expression Kit).
Mix well by flicking the tube to ensure homogeneity.
Briefly spin the tubes to collect the sample at the bottom.
Incubate the sample in a thermal cycler at 16°C overnight with heated lid off.
Add 5 μl of 10X Antarctic phosphatase buffer to the sample.
Mix by pipetting up and down.
Add 2.5 μl of Superasin RNase Inhibitor.
Mix by pipetting up and down.
Add 2.5 μl of Antarctic phosphatase enzyme; mix by pipetting up and down.
Add 20 μl of nuclease-free H2O; mix by pipetting up and down.
Incubate sample at 37°C for an hour.
Transfer the reaction to a 1.5 ml Eppendorf tube.
Add 150 μl of nuclease-free H2O; then add 100 μl of 100 mM Tris pH8; mix by pipetting up and down.
Add 300 μl of phenol:chloroform:isoamyl alcohol mix. Vortex.
Spin at 14000 rpm, for 10 min, at 4°C.
Transfer the supernatant to a new 1.5 ml tube.
Add 30 μl of 3M sodium acetate, 3 μl of glycogen and 900 μl of 100% ethanol.
Incubate at -20°C overnight or at -80°C for an hour.
Spin at 14000 rpm, for 15 min, at 4°C.
Remove supernatant; then add 1 ml of 70% ethanol to wash the pellet.
Spin at 14000 rpm, for 15 min, at 4°C.
Remove supernatant; spin briefly to collect excess 70% ethanol at the bottom of the tube. Remove the residual ethanol using a p10 tip.
Dissolve the RNA pellet in 3 μl of H2O.
Add 2 μl of adaptor mix A to the RNA.
Add 3 μl of hybridization buffer to the RNA.
Mix by pipetting up and down.
Heat the tube to 65°C for 10 minutes in a thermal cycler.
Incubate at 16°C for 5 minutes.
Place the sample on ice.
Add 10 μl of 2X ligation buffer slowly.
Add 2 μl of the ligation enzyme mix.
Mix well by flicking the tube.
Briefly spin the tubes to collect the sample at the bottom.
Incubate the sample in a thermal cycler at 16°C overnight with the heated lid off.
Add 20 μl of RT master mix to the sample.
Mix by pipetting up and down several times and flicking the tube.
Spin briefly to bring the contents to the bottom of the tube.
Place the tubes at 42°C for 30 minutes in a thermal cycler.
Transfer 10 μl of the RT reaction to a new tube.
Add 1 μl of RNase H to the new tube.
Mix by flicking the tube.
Briefly spin down the contents.
Incubate the tubes at 37°C for 30 minutes.
Prepare the PCR master mix on ice in a new tube.
Add 38.9 μl of H2O, then add 5 μl of 10X PCR buffer I, then add 1 μl of PCR primers, then add 4 μl of 2.5 mM dNTP, then add 0.6 μl of AmpliTaq polymerase.
Add 49.5 μl of the PCR master mix to a thin wall 200 μl PCR tube.
Add 0.5 μl of the RNase H treated sample to the PCR tube.
Vortex briefly to mix.
Spin down the contents.
Place the tubes in a thermal cycler.
Run the program at 95°C for 5 minutes.
Cycle through 30 cycles of 95°C for 30 seconds, then 62°C for 30 seconds, followed by 72°C for 30 seconds.
Pause the program at 72°C after 15 cycles.
Transfer 10 μl of the PCR reaction to a new tube.
Place the tube on ice.
Un-pause the program and repeat the procedure for 20, 25, and 30 cycles.
Load 10 μl of 100bp ladder into one well.
Load 10 μl of 1:10 diluted 50bp ladder into another well.
Add 2 μl of gel loading solution to the PCR product.
Load the sample into a single well in a 6% native polyacrylamide gel.
Skip at least one lane between the sample and the ladders.
Run the gel at approximately 120V until the lower blue dye is near the bottom of the gel.
Peel the gel off the glass plates onto a piece of saran wrap.
Add 1:1000 diluted ethidium bromide over the gel.
Cover the gel with another piece of saran wrap so that it is sandwiched between two pieces.
Smooth out the gel to ensure even distribution of ethidium bromide across the gel.
Stain the gel for 5 minutes.
Visualize the gel under UV.
Choose the lowest PCR cycle showing a smear between 200 and 300 bases for large-scale PCR amplification.
Prepare the PCR master mix on ice in a new tube: add 77.8 ul of H2O, then 10 ul of 10X PCR buffer I, then 2 ul of PCR primers, then 8 ul of 2.5 mM dNTP, then 1.2 ul of AmpliTaq polymerase.
Add 99 ul of the master mix to a thin wall 200 ul PCR tube and 1 ul of RNase H treated sample.
Vortex briefly to mix; then spin down the contents.
Place the tubes in a thermal cycler: run at 95°C for 5 min, followed by X cycles of 95°C (30 sec), 62°C (30 sec), and 72°C (30 sec); then hold at 72°C for 7 min.
Pool replicate large-scale PCR reactions from the same sample together.
Add 5 volumes of buffer PB to the sample.
Mix by pipetting up and down several times.
Add 750 μl of the sample to a MinElute column (Qiagen).
Spin at 14000 rpm for 1 minute.
Load the sample multiple times through the column until all samples have passed through.
Add 750 μl of buffer PE to the column (add ethanol prior to using PE).
Spin at 14000 rpm for 1 minute.
Spin at 14000 rpm for 1 minute to dry the column.
Elute in 2X 20 μl of nuclease-free H2O in a new 1.5 ml tube.
Add 8 μl of gel loading dye to 40 μl of eluted PCR product.
Load 10 μl of 100 bp ladder into separate wells on a 6% native PAGE gel.
Load 10 μl of a 1:10 diluted 50 bp ladder into another well in the same gel.
Skip at least one lane between the sample and the ladders.
Add 12 μl of PCR product into one well in a 6% native PAGE gel.
Continue loading wells until all samples are loaded.
Run the gel at approximately 120V until the lower blue dye reaches near the bottom of the gel.
Peel the gel off the glass plates onto a piece of saran wrap.
Add ethidium bromide diluted to 1:1000 over the gel.
Cover the gel with another piece of saran wrap, sandwiching it between two pieces of saran wrap.
Smooth out the gel so that the ethidium bromide is evenly spread across the gel.
Stain the gel for 5 minutes under long UV light.
Use a sterile scalpel to cut out a gel slice between 150 bases and 250 bases for all samples, changing scalpels between different samples to avoid contamination.
Puncture the bottom of an RNase-free 600ul tube 2-3 times using a 18.5G needle; then place this tube in a 1.5ml eppendorf tube.
Transfer the cut gel slice into the punctured 600ul tube and spin at 14000rpm for 1 minute to shred the gel slices.
Add 300ul of gel elution buffer to the shredded gel; incubate overnight at room temperature.
Transfer 300ul of the gel elution buffer into a new tube on ice.
Add another 300ul of gel elution buffer to the shredded gel; incubate for 2 hours at room temperature.
Cut the end of a 1ml pipette tip.
Use the modified pipette tip to transfer elution buffer from the first overnight incubation into a Costar® Spin-X® centrifuge tube filter.
Spin at 10000rpm for 2min in a centrifuge.
Transfer elution buffer from the second incubation into another Spin-X® centrifuge tube filter.
Spin at 10000rpm for 2min in a centrifuge.
Add 6ul of glycogen to the filtered elution buffer.
Add 450ul of isopropanol to the elution buffer containing glycogen.
Incubate at room temperature for 10min.
Spin at 14000rpm for 20min.
Remove the supernatant from the centrifuge tube.
Add 1ml of 70% ethanol to the pellet.
Gently pipette the solution up and down without disturbing the pellet.
Remove the 70% ethanol.
Repeat the addition and removal of 70% ethanol three times.
Dissolve the DNA pellet in 5ul of water.
Pool DNA from the same sample together into one tube.
Quantitate the amount of DNA present by nanodrop.
Check the size of the library using Agilent Bioanalyzer.
Transfer 2ul of the cDNA library to a new tube.
Add 2ul of H2O to the tube containing the cDNA library.
Add 1ul of salt solution (TOPO TA cloning kit, Invitrogen) to the mixture.
Add 1ul of vector (TOPO TA cloning kit, Invitrogen) to the mixture.
Mix by flicking the tube.
Briefly spin the tube.
Incubate on benchtop for an hour.
Transform 2 μl of the reaction into Top10 competent cells (Invitrogen) by following the manufacturer’s instructions.
Pick 20 colonies to send for CE sequencing.
Prepare libraries for SOLiD™ ABI cluster generation and sequencing following the manufacturer’s standard protocols.
Map sequenced reads to the yeast genome and transcriptome.
